## Natural history notes

A very large wading bird characterized by its blue-gray body, long neck, long legs, dagger-like bill, and dark head plume, often standing with its neck folded in an “S” shape. In Florida, it is found in marshes, swamps, ponds, lakes, rivers, mangroves, tidal flats, shorelines, roadside canals, and other shallow-water habitats. It feeds mainly on fish, frogs, crayfish, small reptiles, insects, and other aquatic animals, usually hunting by standing still or slowly stalking through shallow water before striking quickly with its bill.
